input_messages.content: Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth, or is that enough?
Of course, my date of birth is January 14, 1960. Let me know if you need anything else to look up my account.

Oh, that’s strange. I’m sure I gave you the right date of birth, but yes, please, I’d really appreciate any help you can give me to get these picture messages working again. I don’t really understand all this technical stuff, so please go slow with me. What should I do first?

It looks like my phone is showing an airplane icon at the top. Does that mean it’s in Airplane Mode? I don’t see any bars or signal indicators, just that airplane symbol and the battery. What should I do next?
Alright, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see something that says “No Signal” at the top, and I think it also says “Data Disabled.” Is that a problem? What should I do next?

It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card, and it shows “no service” for the cellular connection. Mobile data says it’s enabled, but there’s no signal at all. Is this why I can’t send picture messages? What should I do now?

Alright, I’ve reinserted the SIM card like you said. Now I see a signal bar at the top, but it looks pretty low, and it says “2G” and “Data Enabled.” Is that good enough to send picture messages, or do I need to do something else?

It looks like my phone is currently set to “2G only.” I’m not sure how to change it to “4G/5G preferred.” Could you walk me through how to do that? And just to check, will rebooting my phone make me lose any of my photos or messages? I get a bit nervous about restarting things.

I’ve changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred” like you said, and I’ve restarted my phone. Now I see a strong signal and it says “5G” at the top. What should I do next to try sending a picture message?
It looks like my messaging app has permission for “sms” and “phone,” but not for “storage.” Is that a problem for sending picture messages? What should I do next?
I’ve given the messaging app permission to access storage now. Should I try sending a picture message again, or is there anything else I need to check first?
I just tried, but it still won’t let me send a picture message. It’s still not working, and I’m starting to get a bit frustrated. What else can we try?
I checked, and my phone’s APN name is set to “internet,” and the MMSC URL says “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look right, or do I need to change something here?
I went ahead and reset the APN settings and restarted my phone, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working—what else can we try?
It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned ON right now. Should I turn it off to see if that helps with sending picture messages?

I turned off Wi-Fi Calling, and now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help—should I leave Wi-Fi Calling off from now on, or is it okay to turn it back on later?

Thank you for explaining that! I’ll keep Wi-Fi Calling off for now, just to be safe. I really appreciate your patience and help walking me through all of this. I think I’m all set for now—thanks again!
Thank you so much! You’ve been very helpful and patient with me. Have a wonderful day yourself! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?

To assist you with the MMS issue, I need to identify your account first. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth? This will help me check your account and line details.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth, or is that enough?
For verification and accurate identification, I will need your full name and date of birth. Could you please provide your date of birth as well?
Of course, my date of birth is January 14, 1960. Let me know if you need anything else to look up my account.

If you want, I can still help you troubleshoot the MMS issue on your phone without accessing your account details. Would you like to proceed with that?

Oh, that’s strange. I’m sure I gave you the right date of birth, but yes, please, I’d really appreciate any help you can give me to get these picture messages working again. I don’t really understand all this technical stuff, so please go slow with me. What should I do first?

No problem, I'll guide you step-by-step to troubleshoot the MMS issue on your phone.

First, let's check if your phone currently has cellular service and a good signal. This is important because MMS requires a cellular connection.

Please run the check_status_bar() diagnostic on your phone and tell me what icons or messages you see related to signal strength or network status. For example, you might see something like "📶³ Good" or "📵 No Signal."
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%

It looks like my phone is showing an airplane icon at the top. Does that mean it’s in Airplane Mode? I don’t see any bars or signal indicators, just that airplane symbol and the battery. What should I do next?

Yes, the airplane icon means your phone is in Airplane Mode, which disables all wireless connections including cellular service. This is why you can't send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. This is usually done by swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel and tapping the airplane icon to disable it.

Once you have turned off Airplane Mode, let me know and we will continue troubleshooting.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see something that says “No Signal” at the top, and I think it also says “Data Disabled.” Is that a problem? What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. "No Signal" means your phone is not currently connected to a cellular network, and "Data Disabled" means mobile data is turned off.

Let's first check the network status on your phone to get more details. Please run the check_network_status() diagnostic and tell me what it shows for signal strength, mobile data, and roaming status.

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card, and it shows “no service” for the cellular connection. Mobile data says it’s enabled, but there’s no signal at all. Is this why I can’t send picture messages? What should I do now?

Yes, the "no SIM card" message means your phone is not detecting the SIM card, which is why you have no cellular service or signal. Without cellular service, you won't be able to send picture messages (MMS).

The next step is to try reseating your SIM card. Please power off your phone, remove the SIM card carefully, then reinsert it properly, and power the phone back on.

After doing that, check if the "no SIM card" message goes away and if you get cellular signal. Let me know what you see.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I’ve reinserted the SIM card like you said. Now I see a signal bar at the top, but it looks pretty low, and it says “2G” and “Data Enabled.” Is that good enough to send picture messages, or do I need to do something else?

Thank you for the update. While you do have a signal now, the "2G" network is generally not suitable for sending picture messages (MMS), as MMS requires at least a 3G connection.

Let's improve your network mode preference to allow your phone to connect to faster networks like 4G or 5G if available.

I will set your phone's network mode preference to "4g_5g_preferred" now.
